newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Spain to back Romania's first-wave NATO bid-Roman.
newsitem.headline: Spain to back Romania's first-wave NATO bid-Roman.

text.p: Former Romanian prime minister Petre Roman said on Wednesday Spain had "openly and clearly" thrown its support behind his country's bid to be admitted to NATO in a first wave of new entrants.

"Romania now has real chances of quick admission to NATO," Roman, head of the Senate (upper house of parliament), said after a visit to Spain earlier this week, when he met King Juan Carlos, Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar and Foreign Minister Abel Matutes.

"I can say that I fully achieved the purpose of my visit, which was to obtain Spain's open and clear support for Romania's goals of first-wave integration into NATO and of European Union membership," he told a news conference.

Romania is lobbying for support to be invited to join the alliance with Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary, who are seen as near-certain entrants when NATO announces its first eastward expansion at a Madrid summit in July.

Senior Western politicians have recently acknowledged the new Romanian leadership's commitment to reforms and democratic progress following last year's elections, when centrists ended the seven-year grip on power of the country's ex-communists.
Roman's Democrats are junior partners in the new coalition government led by Christian Democrats, which also includes members of the country's large ethnic Hungarian minority.
Two weeks ago the new government announced radical economic reforms, seeking to bridge the gap separating Romania from more advanced ex-communist East Europeans.

Germany has no objections to Romania's first-wave admission to NATO, Roman said, referring to talks he held earlier on Wednesday with the head of the foreign affairs commission of the German Bundestag (lower house), Karl-Heinz Hornhus.
"Germany has not made any public statement of support for Romania's NATO bid, but Germany will not oppose if NATO also invites Romania," Roman quoted Hornhaus as saying.
